RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS—AT A GLANCE
STRICT ADHERENCE OF TIMELINE FOR WRITING APAR
The Committee observes that in the respective PAR Rules, specific schedule for completion
has been prescribed. For each stage a deadline has also been given. Subsequent to implementation
of AIS (PAR) Rules, 2007, with the objective to ensure transparency and compliance of prescribed
timelines at various stages of completion of PAR, on-line filing of PAR has been made mandatory
for AIS officers. There is, however, considerable delay in the writing of appraisal reports, even
though there are instructions specifying cut off dates for different stages in the reporting
process. This often leads to delay in promotion and empanelment of the concerned officers. All
the non-IAS Civil Services Associations who appeared before the Committee have stated that
their empanelment is often delayed because of procedural hurdles, one of which is delay in
writing of their appraisal reports and the other is delay in vigilance clearance. [Para 8.0.]
 The Committee notes that the introduction of an on-line filing system of PAR (SPARROW)
in respect of All India Services has been a major step in this direction and it has considerably
resolved the problem of delay. As informed by the Department of Personnel and Training, a
similar mode is likely to be introduced in respect of Central Government Group 'A' Services. The
Committee wishes that on-line system for filing of PAR on the lines of SPARROW should be
implemented for all Central Services without further delay so as to overcome the problem of
non-completion of PAR in time. The Committee also impresses upon the Government that all
the Cadre Controlling Authorities must be instructed to ensure strict adherence to the timeline
for writing of APAR at all the levels. Responsibility may also be fixed on officers who fail to
adhere to the stipulated timelines. [Para 8.1]
PARTIAL DISCLOSURE OF PAR
The Committee notes that in the wake of Dev Dutt Judgment, the entire Appraisal Report
is now required to be disclosed. It has been observed that the Reporting Officers have become
quite reluctant to record honestly the weakness of the officer reported upon, either in a spirit
of camaraderie or not to upset the apple cart. As a result, more than ninety per cent of officers
are now getting outstanding gradings. The Committee feels that this trend of inflated gradings
is defeating the very purpose of the appraisal system as it leads to difficulty in finding out
outstanding officers with impeccable integrity and weeding out the incompetent ones. The appraisal
being a precondition for career progression appears to have lost its importance and this has
compelled the Government to supplement the process of PAR with new tools like Multi Source
Feedback (360 degree) for the limited purpose of empanelment. [Para 9.0]
The Committee favours that the appraisal process should be consultative and transparent
but it also appreciates the difficulty for anyone to be truly objective if his/her assessment is to
be disclosed to the person reported upon. The Committee recommends that some amount of
24

25
sanctity should be brought back to the appraisal system by devising a system of appraisal wherein
not the entire report is disclosed to the appraisee, but there is a partial disclosure only. The
Committee, therefore, desires that the Government should look into the aspect of limited
disclosure, somewhere between the ACR and APAR so as to retain best of both the procedures.
[Para 9.1]
360 DEGREE APPRAISAL NEEDS TO BE TRANSPARENT AND BACKED BY RULES
The Committee notes that the 360 degree appraisal system is a new innovation of the
Government for appointment of bureaucrats at the top level in Central Government. The system
inter-alia includes assessing bureaucrats on integrity and reputation, through a comprehensive
background check, before their empanelment. The second ARC in its tenth Report had, however,
cautioned as under: [Para 10.0]
“In the context of India where strong hierarchal structures exist and for historical and social
reasons it may not be possible to introduce this system unless concerns of integrity and transparency
are addressed.”
In view of the above, the Committee recommends that the entire process should be
transparent and rule based. The Government should frame guidelines on the entire aspects of
the process of 360 degree appraisal and it should be notified. [Para 10.1]
TOWARDS PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
The Committee while endorsing the views of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission
on the need for a paradigm shift from Performance Appraisal based approach to Performance
Management based approach, recommends that the Government should put on wheels the
recommendations of the Second ARC in this regard, without delay. [Para 11]

2. At the outset, Chairman welcomed the Members, Shri Satyananda Mishra former Secretary,

academies viz. Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration and Sardar Vallabhabhai Patel

witnesses to apprise the Committee of their views on the subject i.e. Appraisal and Empanelment of Civil
Servants under the Central Government and make suggestions for its improvement.
3. Shri Satyananda Mishra opined that appraisal and empanelment are two different subjects but at
the same time they are absolutely connected to each other. He informed that All India Service (AIS)
Officers are cadre borne officers and majority of their career serving in the respective states allotted to
them. The Government of India borrows them on deputation and majority of officers prefer to stay in
their States and are not affected by the empanelment process. He further stated that the job in the Civil
Services is permanent and therefore, appraisal of Civil Servants have received less attention as the
officers know that if they could not make to the Central Government, they can continue in the State
Government. He, therefore, suggested amendment to the All India Services Act to make appraisal an
absolutely necessary concomitant or condition-precedent to career promotion, so that appraisal is taken
seriously as is done in the private sectors.
4. Shri Mishra further stated, that post RTI enactment, the ACRs were made discloseable and
majority of officers are getting 'outstanding' grades and therefore, at the time of empanelment, the
objectivity is lost. He accordingly, suggested that the weightage given to performance appraisal in
empanelment process must be reduced. He also opined that empanelment could be done by a Committee
comprising of eminent persons from different walks of life. He stressed on the need to take into account
the performance and achievements of an officer during his tenure in the State. He underlined the need
for bringing further reforms in the present system and stated that the purpose should be improving the
quality of governance of the entire country and not only of Government of India only.
5. Shri Mishra also suggested that, for filling up of vacancies at the higher echelons, applications may
be invited followed by an interview from all India level prescribing requisite expertise and experience in

3. The Cabinet Secretary briefly apprised the Committee about the evolution of the empanelment
process since 2004-05, when there were no guidelines for empanelment, to the introduction of Experts
panel and Multi-Source feedback in the year 2015. He apprised the Committee that the concept of the
Experts panel was first introduced in February, 2005 and the system of Multi-Source Feedback (MSF)
got introduced in the year 2015. These changes were made to bring about minimization of subjectivity
in the empanelment process.
4. Thereafter, the Chairman welcomed and invited the former Cabinet Secretary, Shri K. M.
Chandrasekhar to express his views on the subject. Shri Chandrasekhar briefly narrated the steps taken
during his tenure as Cabinet Secretary to make the Appraisal and Empanelment process more transparent
and effective. He stressed upon the need to introduce effective Performance Management System in
place of Performance Appraisal System presently being used in the Government to assess the performance
of bureaucrats.
(The witnesses then withdrew)
5. In the second part of the meeting, the Chairman called the DG, National Academy of Customs,
Excise & Narcotics (NACEN) to express his views on the subject. The DG, NACEN apprised the
Committee about the delay in empanelment of IRS officers and ad-hoc promotions being granted to the
officers of the service due to ongoing litigations. He urged that both regular and ad-hoc promotions
should be treated alike as both are governed by the same procedures. On a query by the Chairman, the
DG informed about the training programmes being conducted by the Academy and their preparation for
implementation of the GST.
6. Shri P. V . Rama Sastry of the IPS Association raised the issue of two years edge being given to
the IAS in comparison to other services and demanded that it should be scrapped immediately as there
is no justification for maintaining the same. He stressed on the need of maintaining inter-service parity
among all participating services under the Central Staffing Scheme.
7. Dr. A. K. Srivastava, President IRS (Customs, Central Excise & Service Taxes) Association stated
that Central Staffing Scheme is meant for providing level playing field for all participating services,
however, the present system clearly favours only one service which is IAS. In theory, the IAS has been
given two years edge only but in practice it is much more. He advocated that eligibility for empanelment
for Joint Secretary should be uniformly 17 years of service. He welcomed the 360 degree appraisal
initiative and opined that it must be made more objective. He further stressed on the need to decrease
the dominance of IAS in various institutions involved in the empanelment process.

(Central Excise) and IPS association and stated that the OM of 2001 has created an artificial distinction
of two years compared to IAS, which he termed unreasonable, illogical and discriminatory. He also
alleged that all bodies involved in the empanelment process are dominated by IAS officers and thus
discriminatory.
9. In the post lunch session, the Chairman first invited Shri Jayant Misra, Convener, Confederation
of Civil Services Association to express his views on the subject. Shri Misra highlighted the issue of
declining strength of non-IAS All India Services and Central Services officers in the empanelment,
particularly at the level of Additional Secretary and Secretary. He inter alia pointed two reasons for the
declining strength of non-IAS services in the empanelment process, one is the two years edge, which
he termed 'arbitrary', given to the IAS since 2001 and other is all the bodies involved in the empanelment
process being dominated by the IAS.
10. After this, Shri Sanjay Bhoosreddy, Hony. Secretary, the Indian Civil & Administrative Services
(Central) Association, who represented Indian Administrative Service, apprised the Committee about their
views on the subject. He stated that the two tools of Appraisal and Empanelment are important not only
from the point of view of the careers of officers of the Civil Services but also to ensure good governance
and effective administration. Therefore, while reviewing the effectiveness of these tools, a holistic view
should be taken to ensure that the appraisal and the empanelment processes bring out the true picture
of the officers being reviewed for promotion and empanelment. On the issue of empanelment, he stated
that giving an edge of two years to the IAS is a positive step to restrict the gap to two years, as in
practice the gap was found to be much more than two years. In most of the cases, the delay in
empanelment is because of non-availability of APARs and vigilance clearance and not because of any
specific plan or design, as alleged by other services. He further argued that the philosophy behind All
India Services is rooted in the continuous flow of officers from the field level in the States to policy
(and operational) levels at the Centre and vice-versa and the key concept behind the Central Staffing
Scheme is that officers bring experience and knowledge garnered from the field into policy making
positions in GoI and take back the policy experience gained in GoI to the States. Thus, he defended the
dominant presence of IAS at the higher echelons of the Government because of inherent skill and
experience they have, which is not possessed by any other services.

against them. He stressed on the need for providing a level playing field in the empanelment process and
empanel officers based on Knowledge, experience and skills they possess.

from Government, academia, corporate world as suggested by Second Administrative Reforms Commission

suitably designed to ensure downward accountability, towards the civil society. In addition, they suggested

performance management (outcomes) in Government Sector. Appraisal should focus on competency and
potential of the Officer. She further stated that 360 degree feedback should be used for development
purpose only and not for appraisal and the required competencies could be developed with appropriate
interventions for multi-source feedback process. On the issue of empanelment, she suggested that
leadership, emotional intelligence, competencies and resilience are of utmost importance for senior positions
as evidenced by research; Functional (domain specific), administrative and behavioral competencies
needed to be honed for giving direction to leadership trait of the senior officer.

1The All India Services (Performance Appraisal Report) Rules, 2007
In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3 of the All India Services Act,
1951, (61 of 1951), and in supersession of the All India Services (Confidential Rolls) Rules, 1970, except
as respect things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the Central Government, after
consultation with the Governments of the States concerned, hereby makes the following rules, namely:
1. Short title, commencement and application.-  (1) These rules may be called the All India
Services (Performance Appraisal Report) Rules, 2007.
(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.
2. Definitions.- In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires:-
(a) "accepting authority"  means the authority which supervises the performance of the
reviewing authority as may be specifically empowered in this behalf by the Government;
(b) "benchmark score" shall mean the minimum numerical weighted mean score arrived at
for overall grading above which an officer shall be regarded as fit for promotion or
empanelment, as the case may be, to the next higher grade;
(c) "empanelment" means the process of assessing the suitability for appointment at the level
of Joint Secretary and above as well as equivalent posts in the Government of India;
(d) "Government" means,-
(i) In the case of a member of the Service serving in connection with the affairs of a
State, or who is deputed for service in any company, association or body of individuals
whether incorporated or not, which is wholly or substantially owned or controlled by
the Government of a State, or in a local authority set up by an Act of the Legislature
of a State, the Government of that State;
(ii) in any other case, the Central Government;
(e) "member of the Service" means a member of an All India Service as defined in section
2 of the All India Services Act, 1951 (61 of 1951);
(f) "performance appraisal report" means the performance appraisal report referred to in
rules 4 and 5;
(g) "performance appraisal dossier" means the compilation of the performance appraisal
reports written on a member of the Service, referred to in rule 3, and includes such other
documents as may be specified by the Central Government, by general or special order, in
this behalf;
(h) "promotion" means appointment of a member of the Service to the next higher grade over
the one in which he is serving at the relevant time;

(j) "reporting authority" means such authority or authorities supervising the performance of
the member of the Service reported upon as may be specifically empowered in this behalf
by the Government;
(k) "reviewing authority" means such authority or authorities supervising the performance of

3. Maintenance and custody of performance appraisal dossier. - A comprehensive performance
appraisal dossier shall be maintained for each member of the Service by the State Government and the
Central Government in the manner specified under these rules and the performance appraisal dossier shall
consist of the documents specified in Schedule 1.
4. Form of the performance appraisal report. - (1) The reporting authority shall write the
performance appraisal report in such form as may be specified by the Central Government in Schedule
2 and the officer reported upon and the reporting, reviewing and accepting authority shall ensure that
the portions of the forms which are to be filled in by them are completed by them within the time limit
specified in this behalf by the Central Government:
Provided that the Central Government may make such additions in the form or the cut-off dates
so specified as may be considered necessary or desirable.
Provided further that the performance appraisal report shall also be written in such form as may
be specified in this behalf by the Central Government for the members of the Service on deputation and
be treated as mandatory input for empanelment and promotion and placed in the performance appraisal
dossier:
Provided also that the performance appraisal report shall also be written for members of Service
who are on training or study leave in such form as may be specified in this behalf by the Central
Government.
5. Performance appraisal reports.- (1) A performance appraisal report assessing the performance,
character, conduct and qualities of every member of the Service shall be written for each financial year
or as may be specified by the Government in the Schedule 2:

53
Provided that a performance appraisal report may not be written in such cases as may be specified
by the Central Government, by general or special order:
Provided further that if a performance appraisal report for a financial year is not recorded by 31st
of December of the year in which the financial year ended, no remarks may be recorded thereafter and
the officer may be assessed on the basis of the overall record and self assessment for the year, if he
has submitted his self-assessment on time.
(2) Subject to the provisions of sub-rule (4), a performance appraisal report shall also be
written when either the reporting or reviewing authority or the member of the Service
reported upon relinquishes charge of the post, and, in such a case, it shall be written at the
time of the relinquishment or ordinarily within one month of such relinquishment.
(3) Where more than one performance appraisal reports are written on a member of the Service
during the course of a financial year each such report shall indicate the period to which it
pertains:
Provided that only one report shall be written on a member of the Service for a particular
period during the course of the financial year and there shall be a single reporting, reviewing
and accepting authority at each level of assessment which shall be specified in the channel
for writing performance appraisal reports by the concerned Ministries and State Governments
and in no circumstances more than one person shall write the performance appraisal reports
in the capacity of reporting, reviewing or accepting authority for a given period of time:
Provided further that if more than one person of the same superior level supervises the
performance of the member of Service, the Government shall identify the person to report
or review well in advance of the relevant assessment year.
(4) Where the reporting authority has not seen, but the reviewing authority has seen the
performance of a member of the Service for at least three months during the period for
which the performance appraisal report is to be written the reviewing authority shall write
the performance appraisal report of any such member for any such period.
(5) Where, both the reporting authority and the reviewing authority have not seen and the
accepting authority has seen, as referred to in sub-rule (4), the performance of any such
member, the accepting authority shall write the performance appraisal of any such member
during such period.
(6) Where the reporting authority, the reviewing authority and the accepting authority have not
seen the performance of a member of the Service for at least three months during the period
for which the report is to be written, the Government shall make an entry to that effect
in the performance appraisal report for any such period.
(7) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rules (1), (2), (4) and (5), it shall not be
competent for the reporting authority, the reviewing authority or the accepting authority to
write a performance appraisal report after he demits office where the authority writing the
performance appraisal report is not a Government servant.

(2) The officer reported upon may have the option to give his comments on the performance
appraisal report in writing to the accepting authority within fifteen days of the receipt of
the Performance Appraisal Report.
(3) The comments shall be restricted to the specific factual observations contained in the
Performance Appraisal Report leading to the assessment of the officer in terms of attributes,
work output and competency.
(4) The accepting authority shall within fifteen days of receipt of comments from the officer
reported upon forward the same to the reviewing and the reporting authority and call for
their views on the comments.
(5) The reporting authority shall, within fifteen days of receipt of comments from the officer
reported upon forward his own views on the comments to the reviewing authority failing
which it shall be presumed that he has no views thereon.
(6) The reviewing authority shall forward the comments of the officer reported upon along with
the views of the reporting authority and his own views to the accepting authority within
fifteen days of receipt of the views of the reporting authority.
(7) The accepting authority shall consider the comments of the officer reported upon, the views
of the reporting authority and the reviewing authority and after due consideration may
accept them and modify the performance appraisal report accordingly and the decision and
final grading shall be communicated to the officer reported upon within fifteen days of
receipt of the views of the reviewing authority.

56
(8) (a) In case the officer reported upon chooses to represent against the final assessment
conveyed to him according to this procedure, he may represent his case through the
accepting authority for a decision by the Referral Board, as specified in the Schedule
3, within one month, provided that such representation shall be confined to errors of
facts.
(b) The representation of the officer reported upon along with the views of the reporting
authority, the reviewing authority and the accepting authority shall be forwarded to
the Referral Board on the request of the officer reported upon within a period of
fifteen days of receipt of communication.
(9) (a) The Referral Board shall consider the representation of the officer reported upon in
the light of the comments of the reporting authority, the reviewing authority and the
accepting authority and confirm or modify the performance appraisal report, including
the overall grade and the decision of the Referral Board shall be confined only to
errors of facts and the decision of the Referral Board shall be final.
(b) In case an entry or assessment is upgraded or downgraded, reasons for the same
shall be recorded in the performance appraisal report.
(10) The entire performance appraisal report, including the overall grade, shall thereafter be
communicated to the officer reported upon which shall conclude the process of assessment
and no further representation of any kind shall be entertained thereafter.
10. Memorial against assessment.- Nothing in these rules shall be deemed to preclude an officer
from making a memorial to the President on the Performance Appraisal Report, as provided under rule
25 of the All India Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1969.
11. General.- The Central Government may issue instructions, not inconsistent with the provisions
of these rules, or as it may consider necessary, with regard to the writing of the performance appraisal
reports, the maintenance of the performance appraisal dossier and the effect of the performance appraisal
reports on the conditions of service of a member of the Service.

Guidelines for Experts Panel (EP) for evaluation of officers for
empanelment as Additional Secretary (AS)/Secretary
An EP has been constituted with the approval of the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet for
assisting the Special Committee of Secretaries (SCoS) in evaluating the overall profile and suitability of
officers for empanelment at the level of AS and Secretary. The EP will assist in:
(i) Assessing the ACRs/APARs
(ii) Evaluating the Overall Profile and Suitability of officers
(a) Assessment of ACRs/APARs:
For empanelment at the level of Additional Secretary and Secretary, ACRs/APARs of 14 years are
taken into account which should have ACRs/APARs for at least 120 months. If there are gaps in the
availability of ACRs during this period due to the officer being on Study Leave or for any other reason
not within the control of the officer, ACRs/AP ARs of not more than 5 years immediately preceding this
period are taken into account.
EP is required to examine the ACRs/APARs in detail, year-wise, for the batch which is being
assessed, and give its own assessment of the gradings of the officer for each year. In assessing the
ACRs/APARs, EP would be guided by the following points:
1. EP will ensure that the gradings match the performance and achievements of the officer in
the light of the officer's self-assessment and the remarks of the Reporting/Reviewing/
Accepting Authority.
2. EP will also examine whether the assessment given in one or two years by a particular
authority is out of tune with the overall trend of other ACRs/APARs obtained by the officer
from other superior authorities.
3. If a Reporting/Reviewing Authority is known or appears to be liberal or conservative in her/
his assessment, this may be taken into consideration while assessing the ACRs/APARs.
Whether an officer has been liberal or conservative could also be inferred from a comparison
with the other reports on the officer.
4. There may be more than one Reporting Authority in case of some officers during a
particular reporting period. For example, an officer in a State Secretariat may combine
several charges and his work might have been assessed by different Reporting Authorities.
Suitable assessment may be made in such cases.
5. In those cases where Reviewing/Accepting Authority has downgraded/upgraded the grading
given by the Reporting/Reviewing Authority, EP is required to give its assessment based on
the justification given/not given by the Reviewing Authority/Accepting Authority.
6. In case of ACRs/APARs where the officer has submitted his self-assessment in time, but
the comments of Reporting/Reviewing/Accepting Authority are time barred, EP may give its
assessment based on self-appraisal of the officer. The comments of Reporting/Reviewing/
Accepting Authority may also be considered during such assessment.

61
7. While assessing the ACRs of upto 2006-07 (old system of ACRs) obtained while working
in the States, special care would need to be taken to ensure that officers of certain Cadres
do not get either undue advantage or disadvantage due to either liberal or conservative
culture of gradings in that Cadre.
8. If representations of officers are referred to the EP by the Cabinet Secretariat with regard
to particular ACR/APAR, it would suitably assess such ACR/APAR after duly considering
the representations.
(b) Evaluation of Overall Suitability:
EP will do a comprehensive evaluation of the overall profile of officers, and discern their suitability
to occupy senior positions at the level of AS and Secretary to the Government of India. In doing so,
EP is to take inputs from a wide range of sources including:
(i) Past Performance records (ACR/APAR).
(ii) Multi-Source Feedback from relevant stakeholders.
(iii) Any other enquiries/deliberations as deemed fit by the EP.
9. To collect holistic Multi-Source Feedback (MSF) on the officer being evaluated, EP will
interact (telephonically) with a range of connected stakeholders, such as, her/his (i) Seniors,
(ii) Juniors, (iii) Peers, (iv) External stakeholders, and (v) Serving Secretaries. MSF is to
be collected from across as diverse a range of these stakeholders as possible, covering not
less than 5 people. EP is to capture each stakeholder's opinion of the officer in a MSF
format (enclosed at Annexure A), having 7 simple questions to be scored on a 1 to 5 scale.
Each filled MSF form (minimum of 5) is to be attached with the final Pen Picture of each
officer submitted by the EP. EP is to assure MSF stakeholders of their anonymity and
confidentiality, to elicit honest and accurate feedback.
10. Based on all of the above, EP will summarize its overall evaluation of each officer in a Pen
Picture [as per template enclosed at Annexure B] - qualitatively fleshing-out strengths and
weaknesses, based on past performance as well as future potential. All assessment should
be substantiated with reasons and specific examples as far as possible. The Pen Picture is
not to exceed 500 words and should conclude with the EP's clear opinion on the suitability
of the officer for occupying AS and Secretary level positions in Government of India. EP
may also specify suitable roles, functions and domains where the officer has potential to
fit well and excel. This Pen Picture is to evaluate the officer strictly with regard to her/his
suitability for empanelment, and will have no bearing on her/his regular promotion.

Procedure for Empanelment and Other Provisions
1. Procedure for Empanelment:
(a) Empanelment should be considered not as a reflection of the intrinsic merit or otherwise
of an officer but the suitability of an officer to occupy senior levels in the Central Government.
Given the background and experience of an officer, she or he may be highly suited to
occupy senior positions in State Government. Likewise, another officer, in view of the
background and experience, may be considered more suitable for Central Government
posts.
(b) There shall be separate Experts Panel in connection with the empanelment at the level of
Joint Secretary. The Experts Panel will be required to examine the ACRs, year-wise in detail
for each batch and will give their own assessment of the gradings of officers for each year,
which will be taken into account by the CSB(Civil Services Board) for making
recommendations.
(c) Officers who wish to represent specific concerns regarding their performance appraisal
over the years which would be relevant for assessing their suitability for empanelment may
be permitted to do so at the initial stage itself. These would include issues such as arbitrary
down gradation of the overall grade, mismatch between grading and pen-picture, missing
ACRs, assessment recorded for periods less than three months, assessments recorded long
after due date, etc. These would be particularly relevant for the period of assessment that
fall under the old ACR system which did not provide for disclosure of the assessment to
the officer concerned unless it was adverse. Such representations would be first examined
and dealt with in DoPT in the light of factual information regarding any violation or
oversight of relevant rule/instructions in recording the assessments or any error apparent
on the face of the record. Those representations that are not accepted by the DoPT must
be placed before the Experts Panel so that the Panel could take into account any valid point
raised by the officer while making an assessment about his or her suitability for empanelment.

69
If required, the Experts Panel may seek additional factual information from the Establishment
Officer but the views/opinion of the Establishment Officer may not be sought. If the
process of obtaining factual information is likely to take time, the Experts Panel may
recommend deferment of such cases for the time being along with its assessment in respect
of periods of ACRs/APARs which are not in dispute. The CSB may then take a view on
such cases once information is available and make an appropriate recommendation for ACC
orders.
(d) For the purpose of evaluating the overall performance, numerical values of 9, 7, 5 and 0
are assigned to 'Outstanding', 'Very Good', 'Good' and 'Average' grade given by the Reporting,
Reviewing and Accepting authorities during the time period under consideration. In respect
of the Performance Appraisal Reports submitted under AIS (PAR) Rules 2007, the numerical
grades as suggested in paragraph 2 of DOPT letter No. 11059/23/2008-AIS. III dated 4th
June, 2009 will be applicable and will be rounded to 9, 7, 5 and 0 as their numerical
equivalents to the range of 'Outstanding', 'Very Good', 'Good' and 'Average' grades. Thus,
the officers would be assessed on a scale of 9 on the basis of their grades in the ACRs.
(e) The CSB would take into account the experience profile of officers, carefully scrutinize the
ACR dossiers and evaluate such qualities as general reputation, merit, competence, leadership
and a flair for participating in the policy making process to recommend the list of officers
to be included in the panel.
(f) Of the batch strength, around 60% of the officers are normally to be considered for
empanelment for Joint Secretary or equivalent level. For the batches to be considered till
31.12.2014, this ceiling has been raised to 75% of the batch strength. The batch strength
for a particular batch shall be the actual strength, less the number of officers due to retire
within next four years for Joint Secretary level empanelment as on 1st January of the
calendar year in which empanelment takes place. For the purpose of determining the ceiling
on the number of officers to be empanelled in a particular batch, this batch strength would
be taken without any further exclusions.
2. Other Provisions:
(a) 'Vigilance denied' officer shall not be empanelled, which means that they exhaust their first
chance of empanelment. The cases of officers who have defaulted in filing property returns
shall also be treated as vigilance denied, for a period of one year for every default. Adverse
impact of default in filing of IPR would be one year applicable to the empanelment due in
the year of default.
(b) In case the selection process does not lead to adequate representation of categories like SC/
ST, women, particular State cadres, the North East etc. in the panel, the criteria for
empanelment would be suitably relaxed to give due representation to these. For this purpose,
* 'By 1st January of the calendar year in which empanelment takes place' means the year in which the case is considered
by the CSB.

70
adequacy of representation would mean the cumulative representation in four batches i.e.
the current batch and the immediately preceding three batches being less than 66- 2/3% of
all India percentage of empanelment. The number of officers to be selected on this basis
shall not exceed about 15% of the number included in the panel and these selections would
follow the process outlined above albeit with suitably relaxed norms.
(c) In respect of representations received after the process of empanelment is over from the
non-empanelled officers, the CSB will decide them on merits within a period of three
months from the date of receipt of the representation, after obtaining the recommendations
of the Experts Panel, if necessary.
(d) Review will be conducted batch wise. Cases will not be taken up on an individual basis.
Review will be taken up after two more ACRs are added. No officer's case shall be taken

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public
Grievances, Law and Justice, having been authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its
behalf, do hereby present this Ninety-third Report on Action Taken by Government on the recommendations/
observations contained in the Ninetieth Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2017-18) of
the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.

Public Grievances and Pensions was presented to Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on
15th March, 2017.
3. The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions furnished the Action Taken Replies on
the Ninetieth Report of the Committee on 30th June, 2017. The Committee considered the draft Report
and adopted the same at its meeting held on 14th November, 2017.
4. For the facility of reference and convenience, the observations and recommendations of the
Committee have been printed in bold and italics letters in the body of the Report.
N
EW D ELHI; BHUPENDER YADA V

REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of Personnel,
Public Grievances and Pensions on the recommendations/observations of the Department-related
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice in its Ninetieth
Report on the Demands for Grants (2017-18) of the Ministry. The Report was presented to Rajya Sabha
and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on the 15th March, 2017.
2. The Action Taken Replies have been received from the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances
and Pensions in respect of the recommendations contained in the above mentioned Report on the 30th
June, 2017. These replies have been categorized as follows:
CHAPTER-I : The recommendations/observations which have been accepted by the Ministry,
i.e. in respect of paras 2.51, 3.18, 3.34, 3.46, 3.47, 3.48, 3.61, 3.62, 3.68, 3.77,
3.78, 3.90, 3.91 and 3.92 of the Report. The Committee is pleased to note that
the Ministry has accepted these recommendations.
CHAPTER-II : The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue
in view of the replies given by the Ministry, i.e. in respect of paras 2.50, 3.25,
3.39, 3.79 and 3.80 of the Report. The Committee is satisfied with the explanations
advanced by the Ministry and does not wish to pursue them as of now.
CHAPTER-III : The recommendations/observations in respect of which Committee is not satisfied
with the replies given by the Ministry, i.e. with regard to paras 3.4, 3.7, 3.8, 3.15,
3.16, 3.17, 3.19, 3.26, 3.27, 3.38, 3.54 and 3.76 of the Report. The Committee
does not accept the reasons given for not accepting the recommendations of the
Committee and reiterates its recommendations.

2
CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN
ACCEPTED BY THE MINISTRY
DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND TRAINING
Schemes for improving HR potential of personnel working under the Government
Recommendation/Observation
1.0. The Department of Personnel and Training and bodies/organizations under its administrative control
play a very important role in the personnel management under Government of India and in the governance
of the Country. The Ministry was allocated for FY 2016-17 under plan schemes ` 250.00 crores at BE
stage and ` 258.00 crores at RE stage. Even for the BE (2017-18) only ` 340.00 crores has been
allocated under the head scheme. The allocations under scheme head are very modest compared to the
task entrusted with the Ministry. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should devise
innovative schemes/programmes aimed at improving HR potential and productivity and seek allocations
for them in order to improve quality and standards of personnel working under the Government. The
organizations under the Department of Personnel and Training play very important role in their respective
fields of Governance. The Committee also recommends that these organizations should also frame
Schemes/programmes aimed at bringing improvements in their systems, procedures and personnel and seek
allocations for such schemes. (Para 2.51)
Action Taken
1.1. Budgetary allocations to all the Schemes and establishment related expenditure of the Ministry and
its various attached/ subordinate offices are made on the basis of budgetary ceilings approved by M/o
Finance on the basis of projections made by the line Ministry to the Ministry of Finance and on the basis
of the discussions in the pre-Budget meeting taken by Secretary (Expenditure) with the representatives
of the Ministry.
1.2. Any additionality on account of increased requirement of funds are proposed to M/o Finance at the
various Supplementary stages and the Revised Estimate stage during the Financial year. A constant
endeavor is made to implement existing schemes/ programmes of the Ministry in a way to achieve the
desired objectives and results.
1.3. A T oken provision of ` 1.00 Lakh under Non-Scheme has been kept for implementation of the
"Human Resource Management System (HRMS)" which was recommended by the Expenditure Management
Commission (EMC). The online HRMS portal would comprehensively cover all service matters from
entry to exit including leave, transfer, promotion, performance appraisal, travel, LTC, pay, pensions,
advances, etc. DOPT has finalised e-service book module for implementation and on a pilot basis, it is
being implemented in DOPT itself for all of its employees. Since the concerned Division is in the process
of taking necessary approvals for HRMS, a token provision of Rs 1.00 Lakh has been made in BE 2017-
18. Additional requirement of funds under the HRMS would be taken up with M/o Finance at the
Supplementary/ RE 2017-18 stage.
2

3
1.4. The committee's recommendation for framing schemes/programmes aimed at bringing improvements
in systems, procedures and personnel have been noted for future compliance.
Further Observation
1.5. The Committee takes note of the reply.
CENTRAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION (CBI) CAPACITY BUILDING AND SKILL
DEVELOPMENT
Recommendation/Observation
2.0. The Committee endorses the need for capacity enhancement and skill development of the CBI and
commends the proposal of projects like Centralized Technology Vertical (CTV) - CBI, setting up of
International Centre of Excellence in Investigation (ICEI-CBI) and International Centre of Excellence
in Forensic Science. The Committee recommends that approval and establishment of these projects may
be expedited. (Para 3.18)
Action Taken
2.1. The project for setting of Centralized Technology Vertical (CTV)-CBI, and engagement of National
Institute of Smart Governance (NISG) as consultant has already been sanctioned.
2.2. The International Center of Excellence in Investigation (ICEI-CBI) is under consideration.
2.3. Proposal for setting up of ICEIS-CBI is under consideration of MHA.
Further Observation
2.4. The Committee takes note of the reply.
NATIONAL CENTRE FOR GOOD GOVERNANCE (NCGG)
Recommendation/Observation
3.0. The Committee recommends that building of NCGC should be constructed at an early date and
necessary infrastructure created for the Centre to perform its activities in an efficient manner. The
Government should also evolve a mechanism to ensure that the Centre evolves into a result oriented
organization of global excellence which is self sustaining and does not remain dependent on Government
funds. (Para 3.34)
Action Taken
3.1. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted by the National Center for Good Governance
(NCGG). With regard to construction of building, budget allocation has already been made during this
financial year. NCGG will work with the Government to implement the vision envisaged in the report
so that it evolves into an organization of global excellence that can sustain itself financially.
Further Observation
3.2. The Committee takes note of the reply.

4
STAFF SELECTION COMMISSION (SSC)
Computer-based Examinations
Recommendation/Observation
4.0. The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) is mandated for recruitment of Group B and C employees
of Government of India, who form bulk of its strength. In the year 2016-17, the Commission has
examined more than 2.3 crores candidates (for about 70,000 posts), which is phenomenal in terms of
numbers. The Commission has informed that it recently conducted one of its largest examinations, i.e.
the Combined Higher Secondary Level Examination (Tier-I), 2016 for approximately 65 Lakhs candidates
flawlessly, without any glitch or untoward incident. This has become possible by shifting of the examination
mode from OMR based to computer based. The Committee appreciates shift to computer-based examinations
by the Commission. (Para 3.46)
Action Taken
4.1. The department takes note of this Observation of the Committee.
Further Observation
4.2. The Committee takes note of the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
5.0. The Secretary, DoPT and the Chairman, SSC in their deposition before the Committee have informed
that with the shift to Computer Based examination the cost of conducting examination per candidate has
gone up from 
` 100 per candidate to ` 200 per candidate and ` 135 crores liability of examinations
conducted during FY 2016-17 would be booked during the financial year 2017-18. Thus, the Commission
would be requiring about 
` 251 crores additional funds during the financial year 2017-18, as the present
allocation Professional Services is inadequate. The Committee therefore, recommends that SSC be provided
with the required additional funds in the financial year 2017-18 at RE stage, so that its work doesn't
suffer due to lack of funds. (Para 3.47)
Action Taken
5.1. In the financial year 2017-18 the Commission proposes to conduct all its examinations viz (1) All
India Open Competitive Examinations except the Multi Tasking Staff Examination, 2016; (2) Examinations
for Selection Posts and (3) Limited Departmental Competitive Examinations for a total candidature of
approximately 2.50 crore candidates in the Computer based mode.
5.2. The Multi Tasking Staff Examination, 2016 (in which 69 lakh candidates have registered to take the
examination) would be the only examination to be conducted in the OMR based mode in 2017 i.e.
(between 30.4.2017 and 11.6.2017). However, from the next year, this examination would also be
conducted in the computer based mode.
5.3. The unit cost of examination per candidate is much higher in the Computer Based Examination mode
i.e. approximately ` 200/- per candidate as compared to ` 100/- per candidate in the OMR based mode.
The total fund requirement by the Commission during the Financial Year 2017-18 for the said purpose
is projected at ` 279 crore.
5.4. Besides, it may be pertinent to mention that in the Financial Year 2017-18, an additional amount of
` 135.00 crore comprising an anticipated expenditure of ` 127.00 crore towards the Combined Higher

5
Secondary Level Examination, 2016 conducted during January-February, 2017 and `8.00 crore for the
Junior Engineer Examination, 2016 conducted by the Commission from 1st to 4th March, 2017 would
be booked during the Financial Year 2017-18.
5.5. The total requirement of funds under the Head "Professional Services" by the Commission during
the Financial Year 2017-18 is therefore projected at `414 crore (i.e. `279 crore + `135 crore) against
which the Government has already provided the Commission `163.00 crore under the 'Professional
Services' Head.
5.6. In the given context, the Commission would require an additional budgetary provision of `251 crore
at the RE stage for the financial year 2017-18.
5.7. Additional funds required to meet SSC's requirement under the head "Professional Services" will be
taken up with Ministry of Finance at appropriate stages i.e. Supplementary/ Revised Estimates 2017-18.
Further Observation
5.8. The Committee takes note of the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
6.0. As examinations have gone online, the Committee recommends that the SSC must ensure that
software, hardware and other facilities at examination venues are audited and made to conforms to
global standards. Also, problems like server crashing, computer hanging, login failure, abrupt shutting
down of computers during examinations which are real time problems, being faced in a computer based
examination should be adequately taken care of so that no candidate suffer because of this.
(Para 3.48)
Action Taken
6.1.  To ensure a seamless conduct of its examinations, in the Computer Based Mode, SSC undertakes
a comprehensive pre-examination preparedness review along with its service provider.
6.2. All examination venues are pre-audited through joint inspections conducted by the officers of the
SSC and the representatives of the service provider. During the audit, all venues are screened for proper
functioning and mock tests are conducted in the auto pilot mode to simulate near real time examination
scenarios to check the functioning of equipment on full load as also the preparedness of the manpower
to be deployed at the examination venues. The supervisory and technical manpower components of the
service provider engaged on examination duty are subjected to an intensive training programme before
being deployed on examination duty.
6.3. During the course of the examination, the service provider deploys his supervisory staff and
technical team at all the examination venues to ensure the smooth conduct of the examination. Back up
machines are checked in standby mode to take over the examination in case of any unforeseen event
of server crash or hardware failure. Adequate number of buffer exam terminals are tested and kept ready
to manage abrupt shutting down of exam terminals or systems hang issues. Inspecting Officers from
SSC are also deputed by the Commission to oversee the conduct of the examinations at different venues.
All examination related activities are logged in the computer for monitoring, and any remedial or curative
action required, is promptly taken.

6
6.4. The Commission embarked on the computer based mode of examination with the prior approval of
the Government in June 2016 and has in the past ten months conducted seven examinations in the
Computer Based Mode. Based on the experience in successive examinations, the Commission has been
taking progressive measures to make the examination process more robust and secure and is committed
to upscale processes further to achieve a regime of zero tolerance to error.
Further Observation
6.5. The Committee takes note of the reply.
LAL BAHADUR SHASTRI NATIONAL ACADEMY OF ADMINISTRATION (LBSNAA)
Shortage of Faculty
Recommendation/Observation
7.0. The Committee in its previous report on Demands for Grants 2016-17 has highlighted the problem
of shortage of faculty positions in the Academy and recommended that other feasible options of handling
this problem may be explored. However, no progress is visible in this respect and the Committee expresses
its anguish over it. The Committee again recommends that the DoPT should explore all possible options
for augmenting and expanding its existing training capacity at the LBSNAA and ISTM and ensure
availability of full strength of faculty and other supporting staff for efficient functioning of these
training Institutes. (Para 3.61)
Action Taken
7.1. The Department and the Academy have been making sincere efforts to attract both serving officers
(under Central Staffing Scheme) as well as academic faculty to serve at the Academy. However, given
the shortfall, there may be a case for providing additional incentives to attract officers and academicians
to come and serve the Academy.
7.2. W ith the existing infrastructural facilities as well as the available faculty/supporting staff, ISTM has
been meeting the target of executing the Cadre Training Plan for Central Secretariat Service and Central
Secretariat Stenographers Service as set forth, besides conducting other calendared programmes on a
regular basis. During 2016-17, 6608 participants have been trained by ISTM inclusive of 2230 personnel
belonging to CSS and CSSS cadre.
Further Observation
7.3. The Committee takes note of the reply.
UNDER-UTILIZATION OF FUNDS
Recommendation/Observation
8.0. The Committee also observes that the Academy has been slow on spending on scheme/plan side in
the FY 2016-17. Out of 
` 13.70 crores allocated under Capital head, only ` 9.21 crores have been spent
and out of 14 crores allotted under Revenue head only 8.74 crores have been spent. In view of under-
utilization of fund sought on scheme/plan side, the Committee observes that every spending unit should
make a prudent assessment of its requirement of funds under plan schemes it proposes to undertake and

7
seek of budgetary allocations to the extent it can utilize. Non-utilisation of allocated funds put unnecessary
financial burden on the Government and, therefore, it should be avoided. Also, strategies should be
drawn for the utilization of full funds made available to spending units and utilization should be closely
monitored to ensure efficient utilization of funds. (Para 3.62)
Action Taken
8.1 Plan expenditure of Lal Bhadur Shastri National Academy of Administration and other Training
Institutions (LBSNNA) was low during first three quarters of the financial year 2016-17 due to delay
in environment clearance from MOEF/forest department and heavy rainfall during the months of May,
June and July which adversely affected the work.
8.2. Budgetary allocation for the year 2016-17 under Plan head was sought by the Academy after
thorough scrutiny of the Plan Schemes to be undertaken during 2016-17. However, due to the reasons
as stated above, the pace of expenditure was adversely affected.
8.3. Ac ademy has fully utilized allocation of ` 13.70 crore under Capital head and ` 14 crore under
Revenue Head as per RE 2016-17 up to March 2017, thus achieving 100% expenditure against the
allocation.
8.4. The Observation and recommendation of the committee regarding projection of funds and monitoring
to ensure efficient utilization of funds has been noted for compliance in future and is being followed in
letter and spirit.
Further Observation
8.5. The Committee takes note of the reply.
INDIAN INSTITUTE OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION (IIPA)
Recommendation/Observation
9.0. IIPA is a premier institution on Public Administration in India under the patronship of the Hon'ble
Vice-President of India. The Committee is pained to observe that such an institution of national importance
is not able to raise adequate funds for its maintenance and performance of its functions. Institutions like
IIP A needs to be protected, nurtured and nourished, but side by side such premier Institution should
become self-sustaining and should be able to raise themselves the resources needed by them and not
depend on public funds. The Committee recommends that Government should render all possible help to
this Institute to make it a self-sustaining Institute of global excellence and for that if public funds are
to be provided for some time, it should be done. (Para 3.68)
Action Taken
9.1 IIPA has achieved robust physical and financial milestones in capacity building and conducting
research in most areas of governance, IIPA interacted with about 4500 officers of the Central and State
Governments each year and renders research and hand holding services to leading-edge sector like Urban
Development, Consumer welfare, Information and Communication Technology and Environment. It has
also established institutional linkages with Niti Aayog, ATIs and Universities through India. In the past
few years, the Institute has taken effective measures to promote and disseminate on the flagship

8
programmes of the Government. IIPA has been trying to attain self-sustenance and is now earning
around 2/3 of its budget on its own. Government is also providing financial support to IIPA by way of
scheme and non-scheme grants for meeting the expenditures an account of salary, maintenance, etc.
During the current financial year IIPA has been earmarked a budget of ` 6.42 crore for non-scheme grant
and ` 5.92 crore towards scheme grant.
Further Observation
9.2. The Committee takes note of the reply.
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEV ANCES
Recommendation/Observation
10.0.  The Committee feels that the spirit of Public Grievances Redressal Mechanism is primarily to
resolve the grievances in a professional and satisfactory manner. The relief and remedial mechanism need
to fix the accountability on the decision making authorities. As in the event of unsatisfactory redressal
of their grievances, the public usually approach courts for redressal of their grievances which increases
burden of courts, every endeavour should be made that grievances are resolved in a professional and
satisfactory manner. (Para 3.77)
Action Taken
10.1. Grievances are required to be redressed in a decentralized manner by the Ministries/Departments/
Organizations concerned. Guidelines have been issued that unwarranted delays in disposal of grievances
may be viewed seriously. For disposal of grievances in a professional and satisfactory manner, guidelines
have been issued that while closing a grievance a well reasoned speaking reply along with uploading of
relevant documents may be provided on CPGRAMS. Officers of the rank of JS and above have also been
requested to review closed cases on sample basis so that quality of disposal is monitored. To motivate
Ministries/Departments to redress grievances not only within time limit but also qualitatively, an Award
Scheme has been launched for recognizing outstanding performance for disposal of grievances by
Ministries/Departments. The performance is evaluated duly giving weightage to the feedback of the
petitioners whose grievances have been closed. Wherever any negligence in taking action on grievance
takes place, the concerned Ministry/Department can take action against the erring official based on
conduct rules.
Further Observation
10.2. The Committee takes note of the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
11.0.  In order to make grievance redressal system (CPGRAMS) more effective, it is recommended that
Government may also consider making a provision for appeal in the existing system. (Para 3.78)
Action Taken
11.1.  Each Ministry/Department/Organization is required to nominate a Director of Public Grievances of
sufficiently senior level who can be contacted by petitioners who is not satisfied with the action taken

9
on his grievance. Every working Wednesday of the week has been earmarked for the Director of Public
Grievance to hear the grievances in person.
Further Observation
11.2. The Committee takes note of the reply.
DEPARTMENT OF PENSIONS AND PENSIONERS' WELFARE
Centralized Pension Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPENGRAMS)
Recommendation/Observation
12.0. The Committee appreciates the role of the Department in addressing the grievances of pensioners.
The initiatives like 'Bhavishya', 'Sankalp' and 'Anubhav' are good measures and the Committee hopes
that maximum number of pensioners will be benefited by these services. The Committee, at the same time
would like the Department to make more efforts to reach out to its primary stakeholders i.e. pensioners
and especially family pensioners about the latest developments and changes brought about in entitlements
including the additional facility of submission of Aadhaar based Digital Life Certificate. As more funds
have been allocated to the Department for BE (2017-18) towards publicity and advertisement, the
Committee hopes that Department would ensure that its schemes reach to the target groups i.e. pensioners
staying in every nook and corner of the country. (Para 3.90)
Action Taken
12.1. A provision of ` 4.00 crore has been made in BE for 2017-18 for creating awareness on their
entitlement and various pension rule among pensioners. Electronic/Print media will be used extensively
for purposes of creating awareness. In the first Qtr. ` 1.20 crore (approx.) will be utilized for the
purpose.
Further Observation
12.2. The Committee takes note of the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
13.0.  The Committee also notes that pensions are generally disbursed through Public Sector Banks and
many a time the banks do not disburse pension timely and correctly. Pensioners are at times harassed
by these banks and their grievances with them remain unresolved. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that Department should also take up the matter with these banks, so that the pensioners' grievances
pertaining to the disbursing banks, are also satisfactorily resolved. (Para 3.91)
Action Taken
13.1. Department of Financial Services (DFS) has been requested to advise all public sector Banks to
redress the grievances of pensioners on priority and also adhere to the guidelines issued by this Department
for timely disposal of grievances vide OM No. dt. 17.05.2017 (copy enclosed)-Annexure-I.

10
Further Observation
13.2. The Committee takes note of the reply. The Committee however wishes that Department
of Pensions and Pensioners Welfare keep pursuing with the DFS so that the pensioners are not
harassed on this account.
Recommendation/Observation
14.0. The Committee feels that filling of pension forms and pension procedures still remain complicated,
even though some welcome steps have been taken by the Department in this regard. The Committee
recommends that number of pension forms should be further rationalized/reduced and simplified. For
this, the Department may consider taking the services of National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG).
The Department may also provide option of filling online application for pension and other pensionary
benefits. (Para 3.92)
Action Taken
14.1. National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) has been requested to examine whether there is
any further scope for simplification vide letter No.2(II)/2/2017PandPW(Coord) dated 14.06.2017 (copy
enclosed)-Annexure-II. Further, it is also stated that through BHA VISHYA software -on-line Pension
Sanction and Payment Tracking System, the pension process has been digitized. Use of BHAVISHYA has
rendered the use of pension forms redundant. Information such as names of nominees and members of
family, bank details for receiving pension, photographs etc., is filled in by the pensioner in an information
sheet. This information is used by the system and all required forms are generated and auto-filled in by
the BHA VISHYA software. Similarly, information to be filled in the Office is picked by the software from
the salary details of the employee and all forms to be filled by the Office are auto-generated by the
software. Therefore, in effect there is no additional burden on the pensioner for filling up forms. Once
the process of generation of e-PPO is in place there would be no further need to generate manual copies
of forms for various authorities.
Further Observation
14.2. The Committee takes note of the reply.

CHAPTER-II
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE
TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE REPLIES GIVEN BY THE MINISTRY
DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND TRAINING
Under-utilization of funds
Recommendation/Observation
1.0. The Committee after analyzing the trend of expenditure in the 2016-17 in the Departments of this
Ministry and their organizations observes that as on 31st January, 2017 the Ministry has been able to
spend only about 70% of the funds under plan schemes. Thus, performance of the Departments in terms
of utilization of funds under plan schemes leaves much to be desired. The reasons cited by the Ministry
for under-utilization of funds are administrative and procedural which could have been avoided. This
also shows that a focused planning and close monitoring of utilization of funds, is required on part of
the Ministry. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should identify the bottlenecks
responsible for not being able to utilize optimally the funds at its disposal and take remedial measures
so as to improve its performance in utilization of plan funds in the future. (Para 2.50)
Action Taken
1.1. Expenditure incurred in the financial year 2016-17 is ` 248.43 Crores against the Final Grant
2016-17 of Plan allocation of ` 248.76 Crores which is 99.87 % of the Final Grant allocations. The funds
are released to the executing agencies by the Budget Controlling authorities as per the demands raised
by the agencies.
1.2. It is also submitted that the expenditure incurred in the Ministry is reviewed weekly in the Senior
Officers Meeting chaired by Secretary (P) and suitable instructions and advisories are issued throughout
the year to avoid savings/excess of expenditure and maintain a balanced pace of expenditure.
1.3. A consistent effort is being made to utilize the allocated funds in most efficient way, as advised by
the Standing Committee.
Further Observation
1.4. The Committee takes note of the reply. However, every Department should ensure early
commencement of its schemes/projects to ensure that 50% of the funds are utilized before
September of each year so as to avoid fund reduction by the Ministry of Finance at RE stage.
CENTRAL ADMINISTRATIVE TRIBUNAL (CAT)
Recommendation/Observation
2.0. CAT has been envisaged to provide cheaper and faster adjudication of employees' grievances
against the Government. This, on other hand, was also to help in reducing the burden of Higher Courts
of the Country who were already under tremendous pressure due to their twin problems of pendency and
vacancy. Even after thirty years of its establishment, CAT lacks physical as well as human infrastructure.
11

12
Nine Benches are not having their own building and more than 30% of Members have not been
appointed. The Committee in its previous report on Demands for Grants 2016-17 had also given
recommendations for strengthening CAT in terms of infrastructure and human resource. The Committee
once again reiterates that proper infrastructure in terms of physical as well as human, should be provided
to CAT, to achieve the desired level of performance. Going by the present pace of efforts, the situation
is unlikely to improve as is evident from the fact that there are about 30% vacant positions and only
about 12 crores has been earmarked for infrastructure development.

the purpose for which it was established. (Para 3.25)

to time.
2.2. There are 66 sanctioned posts of Hon'ble Chairman/ Members (33-Judicial and 33-Administrative).

Lucknow Bench:- Proposal will be sent after plan approval by the Hon'ble Chairman.
Guwahati Bench:- Proposal will be sent after receipt of fresh estimate from CPWD.

UNION PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION (UPSC)
Recommendation/Observation
3.0. The Committee also recommends that the recruiting agencies like UPSC, SSC should shorten their
recruitment process to the extent possible so that the time between requisition of vacancies and sending

13
of recommendations of the recruitment agency is reduced to the minimal possible time. This would ensure
that even the recruitment against the vacancies which are not anticipated in advance is also not delayed
unduly. (Para 3.39)
Action Taken
3.1. To expedite the process of examination of DPC/Deputation proposals in general for appointment on
promotion/ deputation basis, UPSC accepts the proposal under Single Window after scrutiny and discussions
with the representatives of the respective Departments. Considering the administrative exigencies and the
need for augmenting the officers/staff strength of the Departments/ Organizations and especially sensitive
establishments, the UPSC endeavors on a continuous basis to reduce the time taken in processing of the
proposals, convening of DPCs/Selection Committee Meetings and conveying of the recommendations.
3.2. Similarly, constant efforts are made by UPSC to speed up the recruitment process and to finalize
the recommendations at the earliest. The Commission has resorted to the Single Window system for
receipt of recruitment requisition from July 2012 onwards, wherein all the indenting Ministries/ Departments
are required to bring the recruitment proposals in person to the Communication's Office with all the
relevant documents/records for on the spot scrutiny. Further, clarifications on vague terms and clauses
mentioned in the requisitions are obtained from the indenting Ministries/ Departments at the time of
acceptance of requisition itself so as to obviate the scope of protracted communications seeking clarifications.
In addition, the Commission has also resorted to Online Recruitment Application system to facilitate
mechanized processing of recruitment applications with a view to compress the time taken in finalization
of recruitment process. These measures have contributed in bringing down the average time taken in
finalization of recruitment cases. Whereas for the year 2011-12, the average time taken in finalization of
recruitment cases from the date of receipt of requisition was 10.3 months, the same has come down
to 8.7 for the year 2014-15 and further to 7.5 months for the year 2015-16.
3.3. The Staff Selection Commission is entrusted with the task of making recruitment to Group 'B'
(Non-Gazetted) and Group 'C' (Non-Technical) posts in various Ministries/ Departments/Organisations of
Government of India. To achieve this mandate, the Commission conducts eight mandated All India Open
Competitive Examinations. Besides, it also conducts two non-mandated examinations for making
recruitments to the posts of Constable (GD) in Central Armed Police Forces and Constable (Executive)
in Delhi Police. In addition, the Commission also makes recruitment to isolated Selection Posts (where
the number of vacancies is small, and the essential qualifications vary from Matriculation to Post
Graduation degree specific to the job requirements in different Ministries/ Departments/ Organisations).
Further the Commission, on the specific direction of the Government of India, also undertakes the
recruitment process for specific Group 'B' (Non-Gazetted) and Group „C' (Non-Technical) posts in
different organizations. Recently, the Commission has signed an MoU with the Indian Meteorological
Department to conduct recruitments for 1102 posts of Scientific Assistant in that organisation.
3.4. SSC is com mitted to the objectives of merit based selection, and has undertaken a number of
initiatives to streamline processes so as to ensure timely filling of vacancies, with due emphasis on quality
considerations. The recent significant initiatives taken by the Commission in this regard inter-alia include:
(i) Online submission of vacancies by User Departments to ensure accurate and timely submission
of vacancies;

14
(ii) All applications are received online, resulting in faster processing of applications, on the basis
of which examinations are conducted within two to three months from the date of receipt of
applications.
(iii) SSC has made a swift and comprehensive transition in the conduct of its examinations from
the OMR based Mode to the Computer based mode for the conduct of its examinations. This
transition to the automated mode ensures a high level of transparency in its examination
processes besides, the timely processing and delivery of results.
(iv) The Commission also conducts 'documents verification' and 'skill tests' of candidates in the
automated mode.
3.5. Because of th ese initiatives, the Commission has been able to efficiently handle about 2.35 crore
applications in the year 2016-17 as against approx. 10 lakh applications in 2008-09 and also to declare
the results and nominate selected candidates to various Ministries/Departments/Organisation in a rationalised
time-frame. In the year 2016-17, the Commission has recommended approximately 68,500 candidates to
various posts in the Government of India through the modality of All India Open Competitive Examinations/
Non-mandated Examinations and candidates for 384 vacancies in Selection Posts.
3.6. The Commission (SSC) which is committed to the objective of Merit based selection, has by
adopting the Computer Based Mode of Examination, ensured a faster delivery of results with equal
emphasis on quality considerations, thereby compressing the recruitment process.
Further Observation
3.7. The Committee takes note of the reply. It also appreciates the steps taken by UPSC and
SSC to speed up the recruitment process and hopes that these agencies will continue with their
endeavor to further streamline the recruitment process.
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEV ANCES
Recommendation/Observation
4.0. The Committee also takes note of the fact that over the time there has been a substantial increase
in the number of public grievances received by the Department. The Committee desires that all those
areas where large number of grievances are received, are examined and in those common areas of
grievances, after analyzing the root cause, systemic changes should be brought in to reduce the volume
of grievances pertaining to them. Also, suo-motu information relating to those areas should be largely
publicized on the Department's website, news papers and other such media. (Para 3.79)
Action Taken
4.1. A Grievance Analysis Study in r/o top 20 Ministries/ Departments Organizations listed on CPGRAMS
in terms of number of grievances received have been conducted for identifying focus areas where large
number of grievances are received, identifying the root cause of such grievances and for recommending
systemic reforms. The reports have been duly circulated for appropriate action for bringing systemic
changes to address the issues. A Project Management Unit (PMU) is now working in the Department
for monitoring reforms in the departments studied. A number of reforms have already taken place. Some

15
of them are automatic refunds on cancellation of confirmed rail tickets, mechanized cleaning of coaches,
installation of bio-toilets in selected trains, expeditious IT refunds, online delivery of CGHS cards,
creation of unified web portal mylpg.in and mobile app for online booking of new LPG connections,
introduction of e-Sewa by CPWD for redress of grievances, creation of universal account number by
the EPFO etc.
4.2. A Grievance Analysis Study for the next 20 Ministries/Departments receiving maximum grievances
on CPGRAMS with focus on systemic reforms is now at the final stage. The reports will be shortly
circulated to all concerned for further action on systemic reforms.
Further Observation
4.3. The Committee takes note of the reply and appreciates the continual efforts of the Department
for not only disposing of grievances but assessing and analyzing the quality of grievance redressal
in the Ministries/Departments of the Government of India. The data thus collected from various
Ministries/Departments should be uploaded on the website of the Department.
Recommendation/Observation
5.0. Further, as of now, 21 States/UTs have enacted statute for time bound delivery of services. The
Right of Citizens for Time Bound Delivery of Goods and Services and Redress of their Grievances Bill,
2011 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 20th December, 2011. However, it could not be passed and
lapsed with the dissolution of the 15th Lok Sabha. The Committee feels that Delivery of Government
Services and Grievance Redressal should have statutory backing. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that the Government should consider re-introduction of the said Bill in the year 2017-18.
(Para 3.80)
Action Taken
5.1. As per the directions of competent authority, initially before the re-introduction of the Bill, a Scheme
has been prepared for delivery of services and redress of grievances. The matter is under process for
obtaining the views of Committee of Secretaries.
Further Observation
5.2. The Committee takes note of the reply and reiterates that the Government should consider
re-introduction of the said Bill in the year 2017-18.

CHAPTER-III

ACCEPTED REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY
DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND TRAINING
Vacancies in the Indian Administrative Service (IAS)
Recommendation/Observation
1.0. On a perusal of Annual Report 2016-17 of the Ministr y, the Committee observes that shortage of
IAS officers in this Country has been a perennial problem since 1951. But now the vacancy position has
increased to an alarming level. With the present rate of recruitment it will require decades to fill the
existing vacancies. The Committee notes that almost all the key and strategic positions under the Union
as well as the States are being manned by the IAS and persistent shortage in the IAS officers ultimately
affects governance in the country. The Committee expresses its serious concern over persistent shortage
of IAS officers and strongly recommends that all efforts be made to fill these vacancies. The Committee
further notes that the Director, LBSNAA has informed it that Academy has the capacity to train more
than 180 officers, it, therefore, fails to understand as to why lack of training capacity has been cited
as one of the reasons for not filling the vacancies of IAS officers. The Committee feels lack of training
capacity should not become a reason for non-filling of vacancies of IAS officers and if we are actually
short of capacity in this regard, efforts should be made to enhance our capacity to train more IAS officers
and that should not be a difficult to achieve. (Para 3.4)
Action Taken
1.1. In this regard information regarding training conducted at the Academy, its training capacity as well
as infrastructure and various facilities are detailed at Annexure-III and IV .
Further Observation
1.2. The Committee is not satisfied with the reply as it is limited to only training capacity and
infrastructure of LBSNAA, whereas the Committee had observed that lack of training capacity
should not become a reason for non filling of vacancies of IAS. It hopes that the Department
would take proactive measures to ensure that there is no deficit in either of the cadres, so that
governance of the country is not adversely affected.
